o1.biggest_strength: It calls the in-app checkout bug first, sizes it correctly (~1,860 checkouts, ~560 orders, ~₹34 lakh margin), and covers all five chat topics, including a separate firmness test with a 100-night return check.
o1.biggest_mistake: Firmness rating and EMI amount are left as bracketed blanks. Orders per session is the main metric for the size-picker test, which stretches it to 4 weeks, and the bug fix is not tied explicitly to keeping test results clean.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fill the placeholders, use add-to-cart as the main metric where it fits the size test, and state plainly that the fix must land before any test starts so in-app traffic does not pollute results.

o2.biggest_strength: It opens with the in-app bug and its money range, says tests start only after the fix, and sizes every test to the real traffic. It also notes that add-to-cart is the wrong metric for the delivery and EMI tests and uses gross profit as the guardrail.
o2.biggest_mistake: It has no standalone firmness test (only reviews tabs) and gives less customer-facing copy in the brand voice. The dense rules and fixed calendar dates read as heavy.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add ready-to-paste trial and delivery lines in the brand voice and tighten the rules section.
o2.overall_note: More rigorous test design and ship rules.

reason: Both catch the in-app bug, the size picker and the delivery date with correct numbers. Output 2 is stricter about the order of work (fix first), metric choice, sample-size per test, stop and ship rules, and gross-profit guardrails, so I could hand it to the team with fewer questions. Output 1 is friendlier and has more copy, but leaves placeholders.
